plan.angle: The live top 10 is printable PDFs and hospital sheets: a law office's form to notarize, a hospital's grandparent consent, a vision clinic's parental consent, a state signature form, a site selling minor consent PDFs and a health plan's authorization. Each is a blank page a parent fills in by hand and hands over. None keeps the child's allergies, medicines and insurance card with the signed authorization, none ends on a date, and none tells an exchange program which parents abroad have not signed. This page builds the form a parent signs to name the adult who may consent to care while the parent is away (a grandparent, a friend's family, a host family, a nanny), saved as a record the caregiver opens on a phone. It stays apart from the parent consent page, which is about schools and clubs collecting consent for their own activities.
tab_stories: Claire Ashdown leaves for a 10-day work trip and names her parents Ruth and Harold Ashdown as the adults who may consent to care for her son Emmett, 8, with his peanut allergy, his inhaler and both sides of his insurance card in the record Ruth opens on her phone at urgent care.

Daniel Ferraro's daughter Lucy, 11, spends 7 days at a lake house with her friend's family, and he names Elena Delgado as the adult who may consent to care, with Lucy's pediatrician's number and a note that she takes no daily medicine.

Bridgeway Exchange places 40 students with host families for the school year, each student's parents sign from abroad to name the host parents, and by the first day of school coordinator Lena Hartwell sees 37 signed and 3 parents sent an email reminder.
Owen Brack names nanny Marisol Abrego for his children Finn and Hattie through August 31, and the app emails him 14 days before that date so he signs a form for a second year.

claims_to_source: California Family Code 6910: a parent, guardian or relative caregiver may authorize in writing an adult into whose care a minor has been entrusted to consent to medical or dental care for the minor

Texas Family Code 32.001(a)(5): an adult who has actual care, control and possession of the child and has written authorization to consent from a person having the right to consent may consent to treatment when that person cannot be contacted
Texas Family Code 32.001(a)(1): a grandparent may consent to a child's treatment when the person with the right to consent cannot be contacted and has not given actual notice to the contrary

Texas Family Code 32.002(a): consent to treatment under the subchapter must be in writing, signed by the person giving consent, and given to the doctor, hospital or other medical facility that administers the treatment
Texas Family Code 32.001(c): the section does not apply to consent for a child's immunization

Texas Family Code 32.002(b): the consent must include the child's name, one or both parents' names if known and any managing conservator or guardian, the consenting person's name and relationship to the child, a statement of the nature of the treatment, and the date treatment is to begin
